title: i18n (zh-CN): platform-authored refusals and console strings still answer in English — approval record lock, master-record denial, not-found, masked-field filter, delegated-scope, "No options"
body:
## What

An app project ran a browser end-to-end pass on 18.5.0 (zh-CN org, zh-CN browser), and its own refusals (hook refusal catalogues) answer in Chinese. Several messages and labels that the **platform** writes still answer in English and carry no localized `userMessage`. A Chinese user sees English at these points:

| Where | What the user sees |
|---|---|
| Edit a record held by a pending approval (409 record lock) | English lock message, no `userMessage` |
| Edit a child whose master the user may read but not edit | English denial |
| A record id the user cannot see | `Record … not found` (English) |
| Filter or sort on a field the user may not read (masked field) | English "references field(s) not readable" |
| Security admin assigns a permission set outside their delegated scope | `Outside your delegated scope…` (English) |
| List filter on a select with no values yet | `No options` |
| Audit log list → action filter | some action options in English |
| Opening by URL an object the user may not read | 「未找到对象 … 在当前配置中不存在」 instead of a no-access message |

The last row is a wording issue rather than a translation issue: telling a user the object "does not exist in the current configuration", when the real reason is a permission, is misleading. It should say no access, as dashboards already do (「无权访问」).

## Expected

Every platform-authored refusal carries a localized `userMessage` in the request's language, the same way hook refusals do since 18.5.0. Console chrome strings such as `No options` and the audit action options are translated in the zh-CN bundle.

## Repro

A fresh app on 18.5.0 with a zh-CN default locale, logged in as roles without the respective permission. Every row above is reproducible over REST (`Accept-Language: zh-CN`) or in the console.
